meta.title: Tailscale Mesh Deployment: Ubuntu 24 Hosts + K8s + K3s across Hetzner Datacenters
meta.strategy: Tailscale Operator (Helm) on each cluster + host-level Tailscale daemon on both Ubuntu 24 nodes. All inter-host traffic (MinIO backup, kubectl, SSH) routes over encrypted WireGuard mesh via stable 100.x.x.x IPs. Public interfaces fully firewalled for sensitive ports.

topology.host_a: Hetzner DC-1 (e.g. FSN1) — runs k8s or k3s cluster + MinIO backup target
topology.host_b: Hetzner DC-2 (e.g. HEL1) — runs k3s workload cluster
topology.tailnet: Both hosts + operator pods join same tailnet. Cross-DC traffic: direct WireGuard P2P (Hetzner public IPs allow direct UDP). DERP relay fallback automatic if NAT changes.

deployment_modes_explained.host_daemon: Required on both Ubuntu 24 nodes. Gives each host a stable Tailscale IP for SSH, MinIO S3 endpoint, and kubectl access.
deployment_modes_explained.k8s_operator: Recommended for both clusters. Manages per-service tailnet exposure via LoadBalancer annotation without node-level Tailscale on every worker.
deployment_modes_explained.subnet_router: Optional but powerful — exposes full pod/service CIDR into tailnet so any tailnet device can curl cluster-internal IPs directly.
deployment_modes_explained.k3s_native_vpn_auth: K3s-specific: --vpn-auth flag at k3s server/agent level uses Tailscale for inter-node cluster traffic itself, not just service exposure. Use when nodes span DCs and share no private LAN.

phase_0_tailscale_admin_console.description: One-time setup in Tailscale web dashboard before touching any host

1_create_tags.action: Settings → Access Controls → Edit ACL JSON

2_update_acls.action: Add ACL rules to the same Access Controls JSON
2_update_acls.note: 10.42.0.0/16 = k3s default podCIDR. 10.96.0.0/12 = k8s default serviceCIDR. Adjust if custom CIDRs are used.

3_generate_host_auth_key.note: Used for both Ubuntu 24 host daemons

4_generate_operator_oauth_client.action: Settings → OAuth clients → Create OAuth client
4_generate_operator_oauth_client.note: OAuth client is used by Helm chart — cannot be retrieved again after creation

phase_1_ubuntu24_host_daemon.description: Install Tailscale daemon on both Hetzner Ubuntu 24 hosts. Run identically on host_a and host_b.

flags_explained.--ssh: Enables Tailscale SSH — eliminates need for public SSH port on Hetzner firewall
flags_explained.--accept-routes: Accepts advertised subnet routes from operator pods (pod CIDRs)
flags_explained.--advertise-tags: Assigns ACL tag set in phase_0

4_verify.expected: Both hosts show each other in peer list with 100.x.x.x addresses

cmd: ufw deny 9000 comment 'MinIO blocked on public iface'
ufw deny 9001 comment 'MinIO console blocked on public iface'
ufw deny 6443 comment 'kube-apiserver blocked on public iface'
5_firewall_hardening.note: Port 41641 UDP must remain open for direct WireGuard P2P between Hetzner nodes. All other sensitive ports closed on public interface.

6_minio_bind_to_tailscale_ip.cmd: docker run -d --name minio --restart=always -p $(tailscale ip -4):9000:9000 -p 127.0.0.1:9001:9001 -v /opt/k8s-backups/minio-data:/data -e MINIO_ROOT_USER=velero -e MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD=CHANGE_ME_32CHARS quay.io/minio/minio server /data --console-address ':9001'
6_minio_bind_to_tailscale_ip.note: MinIO binds to Tailscale IP only. Admin console on localhost only — access via: ssh -L 9001:127.0.0.1:9001 100.x.x.x

phase_2_k3s_native_tailscale_integration.description: K3s-specific: use --vpn-auth to make Tailscale the inter-node transport for cluster traffic itself. Do this BEFORE k3s install if nodes share no private LAN.
phase_2_k3s_native_tailscale_integration.prerequisite: phase_0 and phase_1 completed. k3s not yet installed.

1_server_node.cmd: curl -sfL https://get.k3s.io | sh -s - server --token CLUSTER_SECRET --vpn-auth='name=tailscale,joinKey=TS_HOST_AUTH_KEY' --node-external-ip=$(tailscale ip -4) --disable traefik
1_server_node.note: --node-external-ip must be the Tailscale IP of this node so other nodes route to it correctly over the mesh

2_agent_nodes.cmd: curl -sfL https://get.k3s.io | sh -s - agent --token CLUSTER_SECRET --server https://$(TAILSCALE_IP_OF_SERVER):6443 --vpn-auth='name=tailscale,joinKey=TS_HOST_AUTH_KEY' --node-external-ip=$(tailscale ip -4)
2_agent_nodes.note: Replace TAILSCALE_IP_OF_SERVER with the 100.x.x.x of the k3s server node

3_approve_nodes_in_dashboard.action: Tailscale Admin → Machines → approve each new k3s node if not using autoApprovers
3_approve_nodes_in_dashboard.note: With autoApprovers set in phase_0 for tag:k3s-node, approval is automatic

4_verify_cluster.expected: All nodes Ready, INTERNAL-IP shows 100.x.x.x Tailscale addresses

phase_3_tailscale_operator_k8s.description: Install Tailscale Kubernetes Operator via Helm on standard k8s cluster. Handles per-service tailnet exposure without node-level Tailscale on workers.

1_add_helm_repo.cmd: helm repo add tailscale https://pkgs.tailscale.com/helmcharts && helm repo update

2_create_namespace.cmd: kubectl create namespace tailscale --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -

3_create_oauth_secret.cmd: kubectl create secret generic tailscale-operator-oauth --namespace tailscale --from-literal=client_id=TS_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID --from-literal=client_secret=TS_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -

4_helm_install_operator.cmd: helm install tailscale-operator tailscale/tailscale-operator --namespace tailscale --set oauth.clientId=TS_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID --set oauth.clientSecret=TS_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET --set operatorConfig.defaultTags='{tag:k8s-operator}' --wait

5_verify_operator.cmd: kubectl -n tailscale get pods && kubectl -n tailscale logs deploy/operator | tail -20

phase_4_tailscale_operator_k3s.description: Install Tailscale Operator on k3s. Same Helm chart but requires k3s-specific kube-proxy compatibility patch.

1_add_helm_repo.cmd: helm repo add tailscale https://pkgs.tailscale.com/helmcharts && helm repo update

cmd: kubectl create namespace tailscale --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -

kubectl create secret generic tailscale-operator-oauth --namespace tailscale --from-literal=client_id=TS_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID --from-literal=client_secret=TS_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -

3_helm_install_with_k3s_flags.cmd: helm install tailscale-operator tailscale/tailscale-operator --namespace tailscale --set oauth.clientId=TS_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID --set oauth.clientSecret=TS_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET --set operatorConfig.defaultTags='{tag:k8s-operator}' --set proxyConfig.defaultProxyClass='' --wait
3_helm_install_with_k3s_flags.k3s_iptables_note: k3s uses nftables by default on Ubuntu 24. If operator pods crashloop with iptables errors, apply the fix in phase_4_step_4.

4_k3s_nftables_fix.condition: Apply only if operator proxy pods show iptables/nftables errors in logs

phase_5_expose_services_via_operator.description: Annotate any Kubernetes Service to expose it on the tailnet. Works identically on k8s and k3s after operator install.

expose_minio_internal_service.description: Expose an in-cluster MinIO as a tailnet LoadBalancer — operator auto-creates a proxy pod and MagicDNS entry
expose_minio_internal_service.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: minio-tailscale
  namespace: velero
  annotations:
    tailscale.com/expose: "true"
spec:
  loadBalancerClass: tailscale
  type: LoadBalancer
  selector:
    app: minio
  ports:
    - port: 9000
      targetPort: 9000
expose_minio_internal_service.result: Service gets MagicDNS name like minio-tailscale.tail-abcd.ts.net accessible from any tailnet device

verify_exposed_services.expected: EXTERNAL-IP column shows *.ts.net MagicDNS hostname within ~30 seconds

phase_6_subnet_router.description: Optional but recommended: advertise full pod/service CIDR into tailnet so kubectl, curl, and database clients can hit cluster-internal IPs from any tailnet device without per-service exposure.

1_identify_cluster_cidrs.k3s_cmd: kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[0].spec.podCIDR}' && kubectl cluster-info dump | grep -m1 service-cluster-ip-range

2_deploy_subnet_router_via_operator.yaml:
apiVersion: tailscale.com/v1alpha1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: k8s-subnet-router
spec:
  hostname: k8s-subnet-router
  subnetRouter:
    advertiseRoutes:
      - 10.42.0.0/16
      - 10.43.0.0/16
2_deploy_subnet_router_via_operator.note: Operator creates a proxy pod that advertises cluster CIDRs into tailnet. Adjust CIDRs to match your cluster.

phase_7_velero_integration.description: Update Velero BSL s3Url to use Tailscale IP of host_a instead of public IP. No other changes needed.

2_patch_velero_bsl.note: Replace 100.64.0.5 with actual Tailscale IP from step 1

ssh_via_tailscale.note: No port 22 required on public firewall. Works via tailscale ssh daemon.

kubectl_from_dev_machine.note: Or use Tailscale operator API server proxy for identity-aware access

check_mesh_health.expected: pong from host-name (100.x.x.x) via DIRECT ... — confirms P2P path, not DERP relay

rotate_auth_keys.frequency: Every 90 days per key expiry set in phase_0

known_limitations.free_tier_device_limit: Tailscale free tier: 3 users, 100 devices. Each operator proxy pod = 1 ephemeral device. Tag-based OAuth devices don't count toward user limit.
known_limitations.derp_relay_latency: If direct WireGuard P2P fails (rare on Hetzner public IPs), traffic routes via Tailscale DERP relay adding ~20-50ms. Monitor with tailscale ping.
known_limitations.k3s_vpn_auth_etcd: K3s native --vpn-auth mode does not support embedded etcd in multi-server HA. For HA k3s across DCs use external etcd or single server + multiple agents.
known_limitations.operator_proxy_pods: Each LoadBalancer-annotated service spawns one proxy pod consuming ~50MB RAM. Budget accordingly for many exposed services.
known_limitations.headscale_alternative: For zero external dependency, self-host headscale (open-source Tailscale control plane) on host_a. Add controlServerURL to --vpn-auth and tailscale up calls. Adds ops burden but removes tailscale.com dependency entirely.
